Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Inc. third quarter fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing CloudForge Inc.'s results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2024. With me on the call are Jamie Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Product Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Marketing Officer; Liam Patel, Chief Sales Officer; and Nora Kim, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jamie Chen.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. CloudForge continued its strong growth trajectory in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included:
1. Expanding our presence in emerging markets.
2. Accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform.
3. Enhancing our developer ecosystem.
4. Strengthening our commitment to sustainability.
5. Investing in employee training and development.
6. Improving cross-functional collaboration.
7. Ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

Thank you again for that introduction, Taylor—wait, no, good to have the team here. Let me dive into our key achievements from the quarter and outline the strategic priorities that will propel CloudForge into FY25 and beyond. As a leading hyperscaler in cloud computing, we're energized by our execution in a market expanding at a solid 22% CAGR through 2028 per Gartner, propelled by generative AI and enterprise digital shifts.

Starting with the top-line highlights, Q3 revenue reached $29.8 billion, surging 32% year-over-year and accelerating from the prior quarter's pace. This beat our guidance handily, powered by 35% growth in Infrastructure-as-a-Service to around $15.5 billion on GPU demand, and 42% in Platform-as-a-Service to levels mirroring our AetherAI suite expansions. SaaS added strong momentum at 25% growth.

Customer momentum is even more impressive. We onboarded 1,200 net new customers, totaling 48,000, with 180 fresh Fortune 500 additions—like a premier U.S. bank shifting 60% of core workloads our way, and a top EV maker scaling edge inference. Annual Recurring Revenue climbed 34% to $32.5 billion, Remaining Performance Obligations rose 48% to $52 billion, with current RPO at $18.2 billion up 52% YoY for solid visibility. Net retention held at an outstanding 128%, with expansions crushing churn.

Geographically, balance shone through. North America at 52% of revenue grew 29% YoY, boosted by AI from Valley giants and pharma firms using sovereign cloud for compliant drug discovery. EMEA hit 36% growth, fastest yet, via GDPR-ready zones in Frankfurt and Paris snagging on-prem refugees. APAC dazzled at 45% to $1.8 billion wait, scaling up our footprint, with Japan telco 5G edge deals and India at 62% growth for customers like Reliance optimizing 35% better TCO with AetherOptimize.

Technically, we launched AetherForge Gen2, managed Kubernetes with H100 integration, delivering 4x training speed over rivals per MLPerf. It drove 40% of new PaaS bookings, $900 million ARR. AetherLambda handled 15 trillion requests up 55% QoQ at 99.999% durability. Sustainability milestone: all 45 data centers carbon-neutral on 2.5 GW renewables, beating 2025 goals.

Market share per Synergy: 18% in IaaS/PaaS, up 150 bps, nearing AWS and Azure via price-performance and Cloud Freedom interoperability for 85% enterprise VPCs.

Strategic priorities ahead: AI everywhere with $5 billion FY25 CapEx, 65% hyperscale for 500,000 Blackwell GPUs; early Anthropic Claude 3.5 hosting in Tokyo cuts latency 40%. Edge/hybrid push: EdgeZone GA in 20 metros like Singapore, São Paulo for <5ms AV/smart city; AetherBridge for zero-downtime VMware/OpenShift migrations hitting $120B hybrid TAM.

Vertical focus: healthcare FHIR lakes, auto ROS2 sims, fin services AetherFinSecure at 1M TPS fraud detection. Sales productivity +22% AI deal scoring. Regional: $1.2B EMEA sovereign incl UK zone, $800M APAC ASEAN/India/Aus, LATAM edge in Mexico City.

Operational excellence: TCO 18% below Azure, op margin 32% up 400 bps. M&A like DataMesh AI, eyeing vector DBs. FCF $2.8B, $15B liquidity.

This flywheel—innovate, win, execute—raises FY25 revenue to $35.5-36.0 billion, 30%+ growth; Q4 $8.9-9.0 billion adjusted to scale. Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Brooks to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jamie. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 32% year-over-year to $29.8 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 71.2%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 38%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us on CloudForge's third quarter fiscal 2024 earnings call. I'll dive right into our top-line results, which highlight the strength of our cloud platform amid surging enterprise demand for AI workloads, hybrid multi-cloud setups, and sovereign data solutions.

For the quarter, total revenue hit $29.8 billion, a robust beat against our guidance midpoint. We guided $28.5 billion to $29.0 billion—that's 3% above the high end and 5% over midpoint. Stronger ramps in AI IaaS bookings via FlexCapacity for dynamic GPU scaling without lock-ins drove this.

YoY, revenue jumped 32% from $22.6 billion in Q3 FY2023—our 11th straight 30%+ quarter, topping cloud market 22% per Gartner/IDC. Outpaced AWS's 19%, matched Azure's 30%, near Google Cloud but with margins expanding 450 bps to 38%.

By segments: AI/ML services 28% of revenue, up 68% YoY to $8.3 billion on H100/A100 clusters at 92% utilization. Wins like $2.5B Fortune 10 retailer LLM deal on SageMaker-like platform, Anthropic/xAI inference; Grok-2 instances adding millions early with top cost-per-token.

Core IaaS/PaaS 52%, +25% to $15.5B; Forge Orchestrator Kubernetes up 40% post-VMware, EdgeForge Zones in 15 metros for AV/5G.

SaaS/Data Analytics 20%, +28% to $6.0B; DataForge Lakehouse +1,200 customers, 35% TCO cut via vector DBs, upsell in finance.

Regions: Americas 62% $18.5B +35%, US public sector +50% JADC2 sovereign with Lockheed. EMEA 22% $6.6B +29%, GDPR zones Frankfurt/Paris +45% regulated. APAC 16% $4.7B +24%, Japan/India +42%/38% Tokyo-3/Reliance Jio; FX -200 bps.

Validates 'AI Everywhere'; $4.2B CapEx 70% AI DCs, TTM $16B targeting 40% revenue. NRR 128% sticky multi-cloud.

Ahead, raise FY2024 revenue $116.5-117.5B, 31-32% YoY; Q4 $31.0-31.5B conservative on election delays, $150B backlog +40% YoY.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Taylor. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI and machine learning workloads.

Thank you, operator, and good afternoon, everyone. Let me expand on one of our most dynamic drivers: the explosive growth in AI/ML workloads and adoption rates. AI/ML has evolved from niche to the heart of cloud infrastructure growth.

Workload growth: Q3 AI/ML compute hours in GPU/TPU equivalents soared 58% YoY, 22% QoQ, on full-year 52% vs infrastructure 31%. Now 28% of compute revenue, from 19% YoY, 12% two years ago. Training +45% YoY for Llama3/Mistral fine-tuning, multimodal doubling compute at 100B+ params. Inference +72% YoY, 62% of AI/ML hours from 48%, for rec engines/autonomous; Gartner says 70% by 2025.

Adoption: 85% Fortune 500 production AI/ML, from 65%; 28,000 users +41% YoY, 1,200 Q3 adds. Mid-market +55% pay-as-you-go; AutoML 40% developer pen, MAUs +37%.

Regions: Americas 54% revenue +62%, tech/finance fraud. EMEA 25% +51% healthcare/auto BMW/Sanofi FedRAMP/GDPR. APAC 21% +73%, Japan/India/SE Asia Tokyo/Mumbai 92% util NTT/Jio.

Tech: UltraCluster 100k H100s/Accelerators 4x inference 30% lower token cost vs A100. $2.8B CapEx to 200k GPUs mid-2025. ML Studio HuggingFace/Ray days not weeks; zero-egress inference 50% data costs cut IoT/AV.

Positioned for $250B AI cloud 45% CAGR IDC. Cost opt key 2.5x scale at 40%+ TCO via distillation/decoding. Hybrid/sovereign 35% deals edge Outposts CHIPS/EU AI Act. NVIDIA DGX/Anthropic $1.2B backlog.

Guide FY25 50-55% growth, 90% top customers. Structural AI shift for transformation. Now, I'll pass it to Marcus Hale for a product update.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched FlexCapacity, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Thank you, Jamie, and good afternoon. Before numbers, highlights on enterprise customer wins and large deal momentum—key engine for growth. Q3 closed $1.2B net new ARR enterprise, +35% YoY, 45% total net adds. Platform strength in GenAI, LLM inference, ERP mods.

12 deals >$100M TCV; largest $450M 5-year Horizon Financial sovereign AI trading on AetherForge K8s H100s. VMware exodus post-Broadcom.

AI: TechNova $320M Blackwell IaaS 10-50 petaFLOPS; MediCore $180M Graviton4 enclaves HIPAA federated learning.

Regions: NA 68% $850M ACV finance/media SAP RiseForge. EMEA +52% $280M EuroBank €150M Frankfurt/Paris GDPR/Schrems II. APAC +75% $220M Nippon Telecom ¥25B Tokyo/Singapore 5G IoT Outpost.

Win rate $50M+ ACV 42% from 36%: AI Accelerate w/Databricks/Snowflake 45-day PoCs RAG; 65% GreenForge ESG; 1,200 ISV Marketplace 22% co-sell Salesforce/ServiceNow.

Pipeline $18.5B +48% YoY, 35% AI/ML 25% regulated; $4.5-5B next four quarters ARR. Avg TCV 4.2 years sticky.

Validates full-stack; $200B+ enterprise TAM Gartner 2027. I'll now hand it over to Sophia Grant to discuss our marketing strategy.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you, Marcus. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

Thank you, everyone. As we look forward, let me share our revenue guidance for the cloud segment and full company, next quarter and full year—reflecting tailwinds in GenAI, sovereign cloud, multi-cloud orchestration.

Cloud powerhouse: 85% total revenue Q3 at $25-ish billion up 28% YoY 14% QoQ.

Q4 guide cloud $12.1-12.3B, +12-14% seq 30% YoY; 45% AI/ML ramp to 22% mix. Nexara AI Hypercluster H100/Blackwell $2.5B contracts streaming/social; EdgeForge retail/manuf.

Full company Q4 $14.2-14.5B +11-13% seq 27% YoY; enterprise software $1.8B +8% hybrid.

Margins cloud +150 bps to 72% Graviton4 40% EC2 25% price-perf.

FY24 cloud raise $49.5-50.0B +26-27% >street 24%; RPO $145B +35%, current $65B 95% conv; $3B EU sovereign.

Company $57.5-58.0B 25% mid; IaaS 52% +32%, PaaS 28% +25%, SaaS 20% +22%, Aurora +40%.

Regions: NA 55% +29% VA/OR; EMEA 22% +38% Frankfurt-3 Schrems/GDPR finance; APAC 18% +42% Sing/Tokyo Tencent/Alibaba; LatAm/India 5% Mumbai-3 public sector.

Bifurcating market AI $100B+ TAM 2027 Gartner; 35% AI inference share >Google 25% Azure 20%. $18B CapEx 60% AI 500k GPUs; 100% renewable 20% APAC cost edge.

Risks: GPU HBM, macro non-AI, FX 40% non-USD; consumption 92% retention visibility.

Executing hyperscale. Next, Liam Patel on sales performance.

Liam Patel:
Thank you, Sophia. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

Thank you, Sophia. Turning to cost optimization initiatives and their impact—cornerstone of our 38% non-GAAP op margins in hyper-competitive cloud.

Delivered $450M YTD run-rate savings, 14% cost/revenue improvement, gross margins +320 bps to 72.5% GAAP. Pillars:

Infrastructure: 65% fleet custom TPUs/Graviton ARM +22% compute cost cut core density/power. PUE 1.12 from 1.24 liquid cooling VA/Ohio 85% renewables Ørsted/NextEra $180M energy save. EMEA consolidate Frankfurt/Paris 92% util Nebula orchestrator vs energy +30%.

Ops automation: 55% serverless Lambda idle 7% from 18%; AI predictive scaling 40% latency cut 10ZB telemetry. Storage tier S3 lifecycle 30% cold 25% EBS cut. APAC bandwidth +15% CDN Akamai peering -35% $60M Singapore/Tokyo; LatAm 42% Brazil localize 20%.

Procurement: NVIDIA/AMD/Samsung HBM3e 12-15% disc vs 20% surge; internal NetForge 40% net silicon $90M Broadcom save; inventory 8.2x from 6.5x trade friction.

Impact: COGS -16% YoY to $2.8B vs rev +22% $10.2B wait scaling; OpEx 34% rev FCF $1.2B +45%. Customer TCO -28% ARR $1.5B expansions 5:1.

Ahead peers AWS CapEx; price IaaS 8-10% below $0.045/hr m7g.large vs Azure; $800M R&D confidential/zero-trust edge. $600M more savings Q4 margins 40% sovereign India/EU GDPR2.

Flywheel innovation/share $600B TAM 20% CAGR. Finally, Nora Kim on security initiatives.

Nora Kim:
Thank you, Liam. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Thank you, Liam. Now on cloud services gross margin—factors driving profitability. Cloud services $18.7B +28% YoY 9% QoQ, leadership hyperscale ERP/GenAI.

Gross margin 71.2% +320 bps YoY +110 bps seq from 70.1%—11th expansion quarter to 75% FY26 target. Beats Google 57.5% AWS 65-68%; disciplined AI surge.

Drivers:

1. Mix shift high-margin +200 bps: IaaS/storage 42% from 48% low-60s; PaaS/SaaS 35% from 28% 82%+ NexAI ML ops LambdaX. AI/ML $4.2B +65% 85%+ margins pharma multimodal 40% TCO cut; QueryFlow 1.2M queries 78%.

2. Efficiencies +90 bps: COGS +19% vs rev +28%. Graviton4 45% new 25% price-perf 18% COGS cut photonics. PUE 1.12 60% renewable VA/IE 100% hydro/wind energy -8% seq 22% COGS. Network -12% undersea MSFT trans-Pac traffic AI; spot/res 88%. Dep/amort 28% COGS $2.1B prefab 30% faster.

3. Utilization +30 bps: 91% from 86%; 18-mo bookings 95%. GPU lead 12 vs 24 wks 110% AI ramps no spot erosion.

Regions: Americas 52% 75.4% +250 bps S&P SAP. EMEA 28% 69.8% Frankfurt 15 sovereign +5% compliance. APAC 20% 64.2% +400 bps vol Alibaba share Jio 5G; $1.5B Sing/Syd 70% FY25.

Ahead AI $7-9B Q3 84% >segment; multi-cloud K8s1.29 AWS Outposts/Azure Arc hybrids. Risks energy hedge 80% 2025 $28-32B CapEx 15% rev; FCF 115% NI. +150-200 bps H2 30% AI mix PUE<1.10. $85B annual cloud run-rate year-end.

Industry-leading profitability scaling. Back to Jamie.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thanks for taking my question. Great quarter on the revenue beat. Can you elaborate on the enterprise customer wins, particularly the pipeline health and any shifts in deal sizes or durations?

Jamie Chen:
Thanks, Sarah. Absolutely, our enterprise momentum is firing on all cylinders. As Marcus highlighted, we closed 12 deals over $100 million TCV, including the landmark $450 million with Horizon Financial for their AI trading platform. Pipeline at $18.5 billion up 48% YoY, with AI/ML at 35% weighting. Deal durations averaging 4.2 years now, reflecting multi-workload stickiness. Win rates up to 42% on large ACV thanks to AI Accelerate shortening PoCs and GreenForge ESG appeals. We're on track for $4.5 to $5 billion net new enterprise ARR over the next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera:
Thanks. On guidance, Taylor, how are you thinking about cloud segment growth next quarter amid potential macro headwinds, and any updates to CapEx plans?

Taylor Brooks:
Hi Mike, solid question. Our Q4 cloud guide at $12.1 to $12.3 billion embeds 30% YoY with AI at 45% ramp. Full FY24 raised to $49.5 to $50 billion. CapEx stays aggressive at $18 billion for FY24, 60% AI including 500k GPU equivalents. Risks like GPU supply and non-AI macro are baked in conservatively, offset by $145 billion RPO and 92% retention. Margins expand to 72% on mix and efficiencies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you. Elena, impressive AI growth numbers. What are the key technical enablers behind the inference surge, and how does supply chain look for H100/Blackwell?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Lisa. Inference up 72% YoY to 62% of AI hours, driven by UltraCluster's 4x throughput at 30% lower cost per token with H100s and Accelerators. ML Studio integrations cut time-to-model to days. Supply chain improved—H100/H200 leads at 12 weeks, on track for 200k GPUs mid-2025 with diversified sourcing. Partnerships like NVIDIA DGX secure backlog.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
